summary:
Heimtextil’s New Talent Area will return to Frankfurt from January 12–15, 2027, with over 30 participants from ten countries.

title: Lenzing pivots to premium as specialty fibre supply tightens
summary:
Lenzing is exiting low-margin textile fibres, closing Austria and UK plants and shifting to branded specialty fibres and nonwovens.
H1 revenue fell 5.5 per cent, but net result after tax more than doubled and free cash flow improved, prioritising margin over volume.
Asian MMCF rivals are scaling lyocell, while EU traceability rules point to tighter certified specialty supply for mills and brands.

title: India’s textile growth hinges on value addition & automation
summary:
SIMA says India’s textile industry needs higher-value products, automation and diversification to strengthen global competitiveness.
Palanisamy urged investment in man-made fibres, technical textiles, recycled and sustainable products to tap export opportunities and FTAs.
Cotton price volatility remains a constraint, with cotton making up 65–70 per cent of yarn manufacturing costs.

title: India's FY27 GDP growth forecast raised to 7% from 6.6%: S&P Global
summary:
S&P Global raised India’s FY27 GDP growth forecast to 7 per cent from 6.6 per cent, citing stronger-than-expected industrial activity, consumption, exports and government investment. 
It expects growth to moderate in the second half of the fiscal year as GST rationalisation and tax-cut benefits fade, while forecasting average consumer inflation of 5.1 per cent and a 25-basis-point RBI rate hike.

title: Giving yarn packages a digital identity: What it means for mills?
summary:
Barmag presented atmos.io on September 10, 2026, as a smart-factory platform for yarn production, giving each package its own production data.
The system links polymer processing, shop-floor data, ERP and warehouse storage to improve mill visibility and detect deviations early.
UNITEX in Trang Bang, Vietnam is fully digitalised with atmos.io and adds 36,000 tonnes of annual capacity.

title: ICE cotton eases after sharp rally as export demand weighs
summary:
ICE cotton futures settled lower as traders weighed Monday’s sharp rise, with volume easing to 52,195 contracts.
US upland export sales fell 4 per cent week on week to 71,231 bales, while shipments dropped around 20 per cent to 142,076 bales.
China’s State Reserve auction sold all 8,049.53 tonnes offered, but the CC Index 3128B and Zhengzhou’s January contract eased.

title: Gildan’s synergy push aims to deliver value from HanesBrands deal
summary:
Gildan has moved into the next phase of integrating HanesBrands, shifting focus from the completed $2.2 billion acquisition to manufacturing and cost benefits.
It is consolidating production, reallocating HanesBrands volumes across its network and raising expected synergies.
The enlarged basic apparel group targets about $250 million in annual run-rate cost synergies by end-2028.

title: AI speeds fashion design up to 5x: What happens to unsold stock?
summary:
New York-based Raspberry AI has launched an expanded platform linking fashion design with merchandising, wholesale, marketing and e-commerce.
The company says brands using it reach market two to five times faster, with sample costs down 60 per cent and photoshoot costs down 80 per cent.
Faster AI design can help test ideas but may also create and promote more styles.

title: Europe's 25 ppb PFHxA rule: Why is textile finishing going PFAS-free?
summary:
From October 10, 2026, PFHxA in textile, leather, fur and hide clothing and accessories for the EU market faces a 25 ppb limit.
PFHxA-related substances face a 1,000 ppb threshold in homogeneous material under REACH Annex XVII Entry 79.
Other general-public textiles follow on October 10, 2027, making compliance a market-access issue for importers.

title: Dornbirn GFC celebrates 65 years and names 2026 award winners
summary:
Dornbirn Global Fiber Congress marked 65 years in 2026, drawing over 400 participants from almost 30 countries to Dornbirn.
Awards recognised Thinkathon, Lenzing Young Scientist, Paul Schlack and Innovation winners in circularity and fibre research.

title: New Zealand’s apparel imports rise 5.8% in August 2026
summary:
New Zealand’s apparel imports rose 5.8 per cent to NZ$180.01 million in August 2026.
January–August imports slipped 0.7 per cent to NZ$1.377 billion as the decline narrowed from 1.6 per cent.
Knitted or crocheted fabric imports fell 12.4 per cent in August but rose 12.5 per cent in January–August.
Apparel exports fell 5.8 per cent in August, though January–August exports edged up 0.1 per cent.

title: Pearl Global commissions new garment manufacturing unit in Bangladesh
summary:
Pearl Global Industries has commissioned a new garment facility and expanded sustainable laundry capacity in Bangladesh. 
The unit adds about 7 million pieces of annual garment capacity, taking total installed capacity to about 108 million pieces per annum. 
The laundry expansion is expected to improve efficiency, reduce washing costs and water use, and generate ROCE of about 18-20 per cent.

title: Heat is erasing 4.1% of Bangladesh garment factory revenue
summary:

Most cooling investments studied could pay back within one to four years; TexPro says 81.6 per cent of H1 2026 value was in the EU27, US, UK and Canada.
Pricing pressure, a 17.4 per cent diesel rise and power risks make passive cooling and shared adaptation finance key.

title: Chile’s apparel imports fall 3.6% in H1 2026
summary:
Chile’s apparel imports fell 3.6 per cent year on year to $1,239.452 million in January–June 2026.
Trousers and shorts rose 1 per cent to $266.481 million, taking a 21.50 per cent share as the largest category.
T-shirts fell 9.6 per cent to $124.179 million, and shirts recorded the sharpest decline, down 14.6 per cent to $70.181 million in H1 2026.

title: Nike reunites with University of Miami in multi-year partnership
summary:
Nike and the University of Miami will begin a new multi-year partnership in July 2027, reuniting the brands 40 years after Miami became Nike’s first all-sport university partner. 
Miami will enter Nike’s Blue Ribbon Elite program, while Nike will supply team uniforms and gear, fan retail offerings, premium heritage collections and Nike Sport Research Lab resources.

summary:

Mapped in Bangladesh lists 2,933 of 3,320 export-oriented factories in Titas-served districts, including Dhaka, Gazipur and Narayanganj.
TexPro shows five product groups make up 79.69 per cent of apparel export value, while Europe and North America account for 86.37 per cent.

title: US' Nike unveils custom speed suit for Keely Hodgkinson

The handcrafted hooded suit features 3D-printed vortex generators, while the new Nike Victory Elite spikes add a tuned Air Zoom unit, carbon plate and titanium pins for racing.

title: Beyond power cuts: What’s at stake for Bangladesh’s RMG sector?
summary:
BKMEA survey shows Bangladesh knitwear factories face severe energy disruption, with 90 per cent citing electricity shortages and 75 per cent hit by gas crisis. 
Knitting output fell around 37–38 per cent, sewing about 40 per cent and dyeing 51 per cent; 87 per cent reported shipment delays. 
Higher fuel costs, buyer discounts, order cuts and loan-default risks are also rising.

title: Vietnam targets $48 billion textile-garment exports in 2026
summary:

Exporters face a 12.5 per cent US tariff, higher costs, fabric delays and uneven order cover for the final months. 
Firms are prioritising higher-value orders, market diversification, digitalisation, input control and ESG compliance.

title: UK’s clothing exports fall to $314 mn in July 2026
summary:
The United Kingdom's clothing exports fell 5.62 per cent year on year to £235 million in July 2026 but rose from £229 million in June.
Textile fabric exports dropped 4.95 per cent to £211 million; fibre exports were £46 million, above July 2025 but below June.
In Q2 2026, clothing exports eased 1.93 per cent to £711 million, while 2025 exports declined 9.17 per cent to £3,013 million.
